title: Content Lifecycle State Diagram
purpose: Content lifecycle with 4 states (draft, published, flagged, removed) and all transitions including auto-flagging on 3 reports, admin bypass paths, and missing state gaps
audience: Developers, QA engineers, product managers, compliance reviewers
description: Content begins in draft state (visible only to creator in dashboard). Creator publishes or scheduled_date is reached, transitioning to published (visible to audience per access control rules). Published content auto-flags to flagged after 3 user reports via content.service.ts:reportContent — content hidden pending admin review. Admin can approve (return to published with reports auto-dismissed), remove (to removed), or bypass directly from published to removed. Removed content can be restored to published by admin. No deleted state exists — hard delete only via DELETE endpoint. No scheduled state — scheduling uses scheduled_date column while content stays in draft. No archived state — no soft-delete mechanism.

actors.label: Creator
actors.description: Content creator — can create and publish content

actors.label: Admin
actors.description: Platform administrator — can approve, remove, restore content

modules.label: Content Service (content.service.ts)
modules.description: reportContent — auto-flag at 3 reports; publish, delete, admin actions

dataStores.label: Supabase DB (content table)
dataStores.description: Stores content records with status field — draft, published, flagged, removed

states.label: Draft
states.description: Content visible only to creator in dashboard. Initial state after POST /api/v1/content with status:'draft'.

states.label: Published
states.description: Content visible to audience based on access control rules (subscription, tier, PPV). Set via status:'published'.

states.label: Flagged
states.description: Content hidden pending admin review. Auto-triggered after 3 user reports via reportContent.

states.label: Removed
states.description: Content permanently inaccessible to all users. Admin action only — no auto-removal.

transitions.label: Creator publishes
transitions.description: Creator clicks publish or scheduled_date is reached

transitions.label: Admin removes (bypass)
transitions.description: Admin directly removes published content (bypasses flagging)

missingStates.reason: No soft-delete state — hard delete only via DELETE endpoint permanently removes content
No scheduled state — scheduling uses scheduled_date column, content stays in draft until date reached
No archive/soft-delete mechanism — removed is the only non-visible final state

entryPoints.label: POST /api/v1/content (status: 'draft')
entryPoints.description: Creator creates new content in draft state

exitPoints.label: DELETE /api/v1/content/:id (permanent)
exitPoints.description: Content permanently deleted — no soft-delete recovery

exitPoints.label: Content removed by admin
exitPoints.description: Removed state — permanently inaccessible but not deleted from DB

preconditions: Creator is authenticated with creator role
Content record exists in database with status field
postconditions: Published content visible to audience per access control rules
Flagged content hidden from all non-admin users
Removed content inaccessible to all users including creator
Deleted content permanently removed from database (no recovery)

annotations.text: No deleted state — hard delete only. No soft-delete, no trash/recycle bin.
No scheduled state — scheduled_date is a column on draft content, not a proper state
No archived state — no soft-delete mechanism for content
Admin can bypass flagging entirely — direct published → removed transition
